inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average ordinary shares FY2025/26 (358.3m basic ex ESOP/treasury + 2.0m dilutive employee awards), FY26 results note 9. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025/26 results: equity-settled share-based payment charge GBP 21m (cash flow statement add-back / note 5). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 across history).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). Model -> quote factor is a fixed 100 (denomination, not a market FX rate), so no rate vintage applies. Magnitude check: FY26 adjusted diluted EPS 15.2p against a four-digit pence price confirms the quote is pence, not pounds.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10-year gilt ~4.5% + ~5% UK/developed ERP x beta ~1.15 (aspirational luxury, single brand) = cost of equity ~10.3%; capital structure ex-leases is ~88% equity / 12% bonds at ~4.3% after tax, giving ~9.5%. One WACC for all three scenarios: turnaround and cyclical risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in a premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full lease cash cost (FY26: principal GBP 229m + finance expense on lease liabilities GBP 47m = GBP 276m, 11.4% of revenue) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities of GBP 955m are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26: PPE 111 + intangibles 44 = 155, 6.4% of revenue; ROU depreciation 220 excluded) so the lease is not charged twice. Company-reported net debt of GBP 852m includes leases and is therefore not the bridge figure used here.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is immaterial (c. GBP 1-2m of profit, GBP 6-7m of equity); no adjustment made.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (operating company - single-brand luxury retailer/wholesaler; routed via dcf-methods table row 2). Fresh build, no prior valuation. EBITDA DEFINITION: ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA post-IFRS 16 and BEFORE share-based payments (FY26: reported adjusted EBITDA 549 already bears the GBP 21m SBC charge, so SBC is added back to the margin and deducted once on the explicit SBC line). Each year's margin is built up as pre-IFRS16 EBIT margin + non-ROU D&A % + lease cash % + SBC %, where pre-IFRS16 EBIT margin = adjusted operating margin less the lease-cash-over-ROU-depreciation gap (FY26: 276 - 220 = 56, 2.3% of revenue; FY26 adjusted operating profit 160 -> pre-IFRS16 EBIT ~104, 4.3%). NOT PEAK-EXTRAPOLATED: FY2023 (revenue 3,094, adjusted operating margin 20.5%) is treated as a cycle peak; FY2025 (1.0%) as a trough; base matures at a 15% adjusted operating margin, below the FY2018-FY2020 range of 15-17% and well below FY2022-23. LAST_FCF: company-defined free cash flow GBP 141m (after lease principal, interest and tax) less SBC 21 = 120; it contains a GBP 41m working-capital inflow that the forward build does not repeat (wc_capture is negative: inventory + receivables exceed payables). Interest income (GBP 23m) is not stripped from last_fcf because net cash ex-leases (GBP 103m) is below 1x the FCF base; the forward build is unlevered so no interest sits in projected flows either way. BUYBACKS: none in FY25 or FY26 and the dividend is suspended - the flat share count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge, with GBP 5m of ESOP purchases in FY26. BALANCE SHEET VINTAGE: anchors are the audited 28 March 2026 balance sheet (cash and equivalents 671, overdrafts 57, borrowings 511). H1 FY2026/27 results (12 November 2026) are not in the Extracted folder; the qualitative file reports cash net of overdrafts of GBP 459m at 26 September 2026 versus 614m at year end. That drop is largely the seasonal first-half inventory/working-capital build ahead of the peak trading half, so the year-end balance is the consistent anchor for annual flows, but if it proves structural it is worth about -43p per share. Replace with the interim balance sheet once that filing is extracted. PRICE: regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance- and recovery-driven base path (10-year revenue CAGR of the base scenario); NOT equity_5yr_cagr
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-9.5% 5yr) because GBP 959m of buybacks and GBP 807m of dividends were paid out FY2022-FY2025 while earnings collapsed; it diverges by far more than 30pp from revenue (+0.6% 5yr) and is unusable as a growth anchor. EPS and FCF CAGRs are trough-distorted (FY2026 EPS 5.9p vs 126.3p in FY2023).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series: CSV FreeCashFlow (OCF - capex) less lease principal less SBC - FY2021 312, FY2023 342, FY2026 121. End-point is a recovery year off a trough, start-points are near peak, so every trailing CAGR understates the forward run-rate; none is extrapolated.

base.margin_note: Implied adjusted operating margin (post-IFRS 16, company basis): 9.6, 11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 14.0, 14.5, 15.0 then flat. Implied pre-IFRS16 EBIT margin: 7.4, 9.4, 10.5, 11.5, 12.1, 12.6, 13.2 then flat.
base.capex_note: FY27 guided ~GBP 120m (4.7% of ~2,541 revenue); converges to non-ROU D&A by year 8 so the terminal year carries no depreciation shelter.
base.tax_note: FY27 adjusted ETR guided 27-30%; 28% thereafter (UK 25% plus overseas mix). FY26 cash tax was only GBP 45m on depressed profit; not carried forward.
base.wc_note: Inventories 401 + trade receivables 323 less current payables 462 = ~11% of revenue; growth consumes cash.

bull.margin_note: Implied adjusted operating margin: 10.5, 12.5, 14.5, 16.0, 17.0, 18.0, 18.5, 19.0 then flat - still below the FY2023 peak of 20.5%. Revenue passes GBP 3bn in FY2030 and reaches ~3.9bn by FY2036.

bear.margin_note: Implied adjusted operating margin: 9.0, 8.5, 7.5, 8.0, 8.5, 9.0, 9.5, 10.0 then flat. Revenue ends near GBP 2.74bn in FY2036, never regaining the FY2024 level.

scenario_narratives.base: Burberry Forward keeps working but does not restore the FY2023 peak. The hero-category focus (outerwear, scarves), wholesale re-acceleration (FY27 guided +10-12% CER) and Americas/Greater China momentum deliver ~5% growth in FY27 fading to 2.5%, so revenue regains GBP 3bn around FY2032 - later than management's ambition. With the GBP 100m cost programme banked and gross margin already back near 68%, operating leverage on a largely fixed store and lease base lifts the adjusted operating margin from 6.6% to ~9.6% in FY27 (H1 FY27 adjusted operating profit GBP 62m vs 19m) and to a 15% plateau by FY2033 - a mid-cycle level at the low end of the FY2018-FY2020 range rather than the 18-20% of FY2022-23.
scenario_narratives.bull: The brand reset fully lands: Schulman's 'Timeless British Luxury' positioning restores full-price sell-through and pricing power, Gen Z acquisition compounds, EMEIA recovers as Middle East disruption and tourist weakness ease, and Chinese luxury demand turns. Revenue grows 6-7% for four years, passing GBP 3bn by FY2030, and store productivity on a stable space base takes the adjusted operating margin to 19% - close to, but still short of, the FY2023 peak, as befits a single-brand house without conglomerate scale.
scenario_narratives.bear: The easy part of the recovery is behind it. Tougher comparatives arrive in FY28 just as aspirational luxury demand softens again: Greater China (28% of revenue) relapses, EMEIA stays in decline, and the wholesale restock proves a one-off sell-in. Revenue stalls and dips in FY29, the company has to reinvest in marketing and markdowns to hold relevance against far larger rivals, and the adjusted operating margin stalls at 7.5-10% - a structurally subscale mid-tier luxury brand. Lease costs stay above 11% of revenue because space cannot be cut as fast as sales. This path remains cash-generative; the terminal value does not hit the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the thesis rests on an unfinished turnaround at a single-brand company with a record of creative and strategic resets, 28% Greater China exposure and aspirational-customer cyclicality, though with net cash ex-leases there is no solvency leg. Base 50%: seven consecutive quarters of improving comparable sales, a delivered cost programme and repeated guidance raises make continued but sub-peak recovery the central case. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs brand heat, China, EMEIA tourism and wholesale all to cooperate at once, and a ~37% vote against the CEO pay policy plus the July sell-off show the market is not yet granting it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Burberry is valued as a recovering cyclical on normalised, not peak and not trough, economics. FY2026 owner FCF (GBP 120m) is a depressed base flattered by a working-capital release, so value comes from a component build that walks the adjusted operating margin from 6.6% to a 15% mid-cycle level (base) over seven years, with leases charged in full as an operating cost and excluded from debt. Risk is carried once, in the scenario spread and a 25% bear weight, at a single GBP-built 9.5% WACC. Most of the value sits in the terminal year, which means the valuation is a view on where margins settle, not on FY27 delivery.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mature margin: each 1pp of terminal adjusted operating margin is worth roughly 7% of base value; the 15% plateau is a judgment between the 10% bear and 19% bull.

Lease treatment: GBP 276m of annual lease cash is charged in the flows; treating leases as debt instead (GBP 955m) would give a different split between EV and equity and must not be mixed with this basis.
Balance-sheet vintage: anchors are March 2026; H1 FY27 cash net of overdrafts was reported at GBP 459m (seasonal low), about 43p per share lower if not recovered in H2.
Greater China and tourist flows drive roughly 40% of revenue and are outside management's control.
No dividend or buyback: the flat share count relies on SBC being funded from free cash flow once distributions resume.
